components.name: Layer Switch
components.description: The signature control: a calm 32×18 pill that turns map layers on and off.
components.css: .ds-switch-row { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.55rem; cursor: pointer; font-family: 'DM Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; color: #2A241A; } .ds-switch-input { position: absolute; opacity: 0; width: 0; height: 0; } .ds-switch { width: 32px; height: 18px; border-radius: 999px; background: #cfd6cf; position: relative; transition: background 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.25,1,0.5,1); } .ds-switch::after { content: ''; position: absolute; top: 2px; left: 2px; width: 14px; height: 14px; border-radius: 50%; background: #fff; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,0.25); transition: transform 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.25,1,0.5,1); } .ds-switch-input:checked + .ds-switch { background: #4A5A33; } .ds-switch-input:checked + .ds-switch::after { transform: translateX(14px); } .ds-switch-input:focus-visible + .ds-switch { outline: 2px solid #4A5A33; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-switch-name { font-size: 0.9rem; }

narrative.overview: LOKA Atlas looks like a working document from fieldwork, not a dashboard. The surfaces are matte greys — the tone of paper that has been in a bag all day — and everything drawn on them behaves like ink: thin borders, earthy boundary lines, stamped uppercase labels, small honest controls. The map is the page; the interface is the margin. The system explicitly rejects the shiny SaaS register: no gradients, no glassmorphism-as-decoration, no neon data-viz hues. Color is committed but muted: a rustic-pastel family (moss, rust, sienna, ochre) that could be mixed from soil, turmeric and leaves.
keyCharacteristics: Cream-paper canvas; pure white reserved for elements that must read as 'on top'
One green speaks for the product (moss #4A5A33); earth accents belong to the data
Flat, ink-on-paper depth: borders and tone steps, not shadows
Two typefaces, two jobs: Figtree structures, DM Sans reads
Refined and restrained components: thin strokes, small radii, quiet states
Everything credited: sources, partners and licenses are part of the identity

rules.name: The Map Speaks Rule
rules.body: Saturated color belongs to data on the map. The interface never uses more than moss + tints on roughly 10% of the screen. If a UI element competes with the map for color, mute the element.

rules.name: The Earth Ink Rule
rules.body: Every hue is desaturated toward earth. No pure primaries, nothing neon, no blues bluer than #5f7f92. A color that couldn't plausibly be mixed from soil, leaves or turmeric doesn't belong.

rules.name: The Cartographic Palette
rules.body: Map-layer colors are their own curated set, and layers ship deliberately translucent (fills 0.35–0.75) so boundaries, land cover and the basemap read through each other. Translucency is a feature.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Figtree for structure, DM Sans for reading. Never a third family; never Figtree for paragraphs; never DM Sans for uppercase labels.

rules.name: The Ink-on-Paper Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest and flat on hover. If a new element seems to need a shadow, first try a border; then try a tone step; only then ask.

dos: Do keep the interface paper-quiet and let saturated color live on the map
Do separate with 1px ink-transparency borders and tone steps; reach for #FAF2DC before a shadow
Do use Moss #4A5A33 for every interactive affordance so 'green means actionable' stays true
Do give every map label a paper halo
Do ship layers translucent (0.35–0.75 fill) with opacity sliders where stacking matters
Do credit sources, partners and licenses visibly
Do respect prefers-reduced-motion globally; transitions ≤0.2s ease-out
donts: Don't use gradients anywhere — fills, text or charts
Don't use glassmorphism decoratively; the ≥94%-opaque layer panel is the only translucent UI surface
Don't add shadows to cards, buttons or hovers
Don't introduce neon or pure-primary hues
Don't use border-left stripes, hero-metric blocks, or identical icon-card grids — the shiny-SaaS register is the anti-reference
Don't add a third typeface or track lowercase text
Don't exceed 6px radius on containers; pills are for the toggle track only
Don't let any UI element outsaturate the data — if a screenshot's most colorful thing isn't the map, the screen is wrong
